subject: Novus Health - implementation playbook & proposed next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Novus Health - implementation playbook & proposed next steps

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. I’ve attached a short playbook that maps the pieces we discussed. High-level takeaways: 

- Primary pain: current summarization service is brittle and expensive at scale (high per-token cost + spikes impact latency during business hours).
- Goals: 90%+ on-target summarization accuracy for clinician notes, end-to-end 95th pct latency <= 350ms for single-turn queries, and predictable unit economics under sustained load (~10 rps steady state with 30 rps bursts).
- Constraints: must comply with SOC2 requirements, change-control for PHI handling (Novus will require a VPC/private deployment option for pilot), and procurement prefers a 60–90 day pilot before committing to reserved capacity.

Integration and product fit items (technical):
- Streaming & function-calling: you want streaming token-level updates to the UI and structured function calls for creating structured discharge summaries. We recommend using our streaming endpoint with funcall hooks — we included a sample streaming-config.yaml.
- Structured outputs: we propose the structured JSON schema we sketched in the call (section 2.1 of the playbook). This will let your downstream workflows map directly to the EHR fields.
- Embeddings & reranking: initial plan is to build a light-weight semantic search layer for past notes using dense embeddings + an asymmetric reranker for recall precision; we recommend 1536-d embeddings for initial POC.
- SDK changes: minimal — we expect a 1–2 day SDK upgrade on your side to add streaming handlers and the funcall signature. We’ve annotated sample client patches in the playbook.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Technical workshop (90 min): deep-dive on streaming config, funcall schema, and retry semantics — target Wed 19 Aug, 10:00–11:30 PT.
2) Security questionnaire & SOC2 evidence: we’ll send our SOC2 pack and an evidence index by EOD today.
3) Pilot proposal: Redwood to deliver a 60-day pilot proposal with success metrics and an estimated cost model (ballpark numbers inside the attached pilot-success-metrics.xlsx).
4) Procurement intro: loop in procurement contact so we can align on MSAs and data processing terms.

I’ve cc’d Ben (commercial) and Sergio (inference engineer) so they can sync on pricing and implementation effort. Please confirm the workshop time or propose an alternative and flag any missing priorities.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments:
- redwood-novus-integration-playbook.pdf (21 pages, diagram + sample configs)
- pilot-success-metrics.xlsx (pilot KPIs + rough pricing bands)
- sample-streaming-config.yaml (stub)

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novushealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Novus Health Procurement <procurement@novushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novus Health - implementation playbook & proposed next steps

Thanks, Olga — this is super helpful and captures the discussion well. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Priority: throughput and predictable latency are the gating items for us. The 10 rps steady / 30 rps bursts estimate is accurate for a single service (summarization). We’ll also want to simulate peak concurrency across multiple endpoints in the pilot.
- Data residency: we absolutely need the VPC/private option for the pilot — PHI scope prevents hosted inference for now.
- Cost: can you include a ballpark total cost range for the 60-day pilot (infra + engineering support) in the pilot doc? Our procurement lead (cc’d) needs that to open a PO.
- Timeline: the earlier we can get a tech workshop (this week) the better — we’d like to start a pilot before end of Q3 if possible.

We’re good for the Wed 19 Aug 10:00 PT slot. I’ll invite a systems engineer from Novus to the workshop (name forthcoming).

Appreciate it — Daniel
Daniel Park
Director, Clinical Informatics | Novus Health
daniel.park@novushealth.com
+1 (617) 555-0172

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novushealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Novus Health Procurement <procurement@novushealth.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novus Health - implementation playbook & proposed next steps

Daniel — great to meet you on the call. Short commercial notes to make procurement easier: 

- Pilot pricing: we’ll propose a fixed-fee pilot option covering infra credit (private deployment on a dedicated instance), up to 120k tokens/day equivalent, and 40 engineering hours of Redwood implementation support. Rough range: $45k–$65k depending on engineering scope and any additional compliance packaging. Exact numbers will be in the pilot doc.
- Pilot deliverables: 1) private deployment w/ baseline observability dashboards; 2) sample streaming integration and funcall examples wired to your dev EHR; 3) acceptance test suite matching the pilot KPIs in the spreadsheet.
- Procurement items we need: PO template, preferred PO approver contact, and any required CLA/contract redlines they tend to request.

Olga / Sergio — once we finalize the pilot doc I’ll send a commercial summary for Daniel’s procurement team. I’ll also propose a simple 2-page SOW they can attach to the PO.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

---
On a related note, Sergio — can you confirm estimated engineering effort for the SDK patch + streaming integration (rough hours)? I’ve budgeted 40 hours for now but open to adjustment.

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novushealth.com>, Novus Health Procurement <procurement@novushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 15:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novus Health - implementation playbook & proposed next steps

Thanks — quick technical note. From an engineering lens: 

- SDK changes: estimate 12–20 engineer-hours for the client-side SDK patch to add streaming handlers and the funcall signature (depends on test coverage). We can deliver a sample client patch and a unit-test harness within the pilot.
- Streaming infra: for a private deployment on a single dedicated GPU node we expect to meet the 10 rps steady / 30 rps burst with tuned batching and prefix caching. I included a reference config in the attached sample-streaming-config.yaml and a short checklist in the playbook for cache warm-up and tokenization settings.
- Embeddings + rerank: onboarding embedding vectors (1536d) and an asymmetric reranker is straightforward; recommend a separate small job during the first two weeks of the pilot to index ~6 months of notes.
- Acceptance testing: I’ll own the pilot acceptance tests (latency and quality). Need Novus to provide a small masked dataset (synthetic or redacted) for the first run.

I’ll be at the tech workshop on Wed 19 Aug and will bring a short runbook to walk through the steps.

Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
